newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end lower on strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end lower on strong U.S. data.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended lower after taking an early drubbing on a pair of stronger than expected U.S. economic reports.
Prices were knocked back early and never recovered much ground after both the June Chicago purchasing managers index and U.S. new single-family home sales for May exceeded analysts' expectations.
The Chicago purchasers' business barometer posted a robust gain in the month, rising to 61.5 from 56.8 in May. Traders had expected only a modest increase in the June data.
New home sales rose 7.1 percent to 825,000 units, the largest increase since November and above expectations for a rise to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 786,000.
U.S. May personal income and spending data, reported earlier, had little effect on prices.
After sinking to a morning low of 110-23, September bond futures spent the rest of the session adrift as selling interest dried up and the market's attention turned to upcoming events, traders said.
The day's data were not seen as affecting the outcome of the two-day Federal Open Market Committee that begins Tuesday.
"Ninety-five percent of traders don't expect anything to happen," said a Eurodollar futures trader.
However, he added that market participants appear evenly split on the prospects for another rate increase before year end amid expectations for robust U.S. economic growth in the second half.

A bond floor analyst said September futures stabilized when sellers could no longer get mileage out of the bearish morning numbers and attention began to shift toward the calendar for the remainder of the week, including the FOMC meeting.
The expectations for steady Fed policy at this week's meeting helped put a floor under the market despite the strong data, he said.

On Tuesday, the National Association of Purchasing Management will release its June survey. Traders said the report was unlikely to affect the FOMC decision and therefore would have limited price impact, barring a strong deviation from the Chicago report.
Key support for September bonds was pegged at 110-15/32, a one-third retracement level from the 2-1/2-month rally.
September T-bonds ended down 18/32 at 111-2/32, and December Eurodollars closed 0.050 lower at 93.90.
